products.description: 100% grass-fed and grass-finished on regenerative ranchland — the standard the ancestral-nutrition world has argued for all along, and the published numbers back it: ~1.5:1 omega-6-to-omega-3 ratio (vs ~7.7:1 grain-fed), 2–3× the CLA, ~3× the vitamin E, ~7× the beta-carotene (Daley 2010, Nutrition Journal). No feedlot, no implants — feedlot cattle account for the largest share (41%) of America's medically important farm antibiotics. LABEL DECODER: 'No added hormones' on chicken or pork is pure marketing — federal law bans hormones in ALL U.S. poultry and pork, and the label is legally required to admit it. On beef, hormone implants ARE legal and common in feedlots. And 'grass-fed' lost its federal definition in 2016 — without third-party certification, it's a self-declared claim.

properties.Why it scores high: Certified regenerative + grass-finished — the two claims that survived the 2016 label collapse

products.description: Farm-raised Atlantic salmon. FARMED VS WILD, THE CURRENT TRUTH: farmed salmon's pink is synthetic astaxanthin added to the feed — U.S. law requires 'color added' on the label. Its omega-6-to-omega-3 ratio runs about 14 times worse than wild (0.7 vs 0.05). And antibiotic use depends on where it's farmed: Chile has used ~500 times more antibiotics per tonne than Norway. The old '10x more PCBs' claim is outdated — feed changed, and current European data shows wild Atlantic salmon now carries MORE dioxins and mercury than farmed. We tell it as the data reads today. BAP certification and Norwegian-style practice are the better end of farming — but wild sockeye needs no color additive and carries the ancestral omega ratio on its own.
